graph.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: The flagged edges were the 8 resistor-to-matrix connections. A resistor lead cannot join the matrix's header-pin ports directly. In the circuit image the yellow wires run from each resistor to a matrix pin, so I added 8 yellow jumper wires (wire17-wire24) as real parts. Each resistor's pin 2 is twisted to one wire's end, and the wire's other end goes into the matrix pin. The resistor-to-wire join assumes a lead can be twisted to a wire-end, as the lead/lead rule allows. Step 1's parts list therefore omitted these 8 wires.

Matrix pin mapping comes from the manual's table, converted to the catalogue's R/C names: pin1=R5(13), pin2=R7(12), pin3=C2(11), pin4=C3(10), pin5=R8(A2), pin6=C5(A3), pin7=R6(A4), pin8=R3(A5), pin9=R1(2), pin10=C4(3), pin11=C6(4), pin12=R4(5), pin13=C1(6), pin14=R2(7), pin15=C7(8), pin16=C8(9).
The 8 resistors are in series on Arduino pins 2-9. Pins 10-13 and A2-A5 go to the matrix through green jumper wires with no resistor, as drawn.
In the image, the upper pot (pot1) goes to A1 and the lower pot (pot2) goes to A0.

The image shows the breadboard rotated, with rows numbered down the side. I read its right-hand rails as 'tp' (+) and 'tn' (-). Rails are single strips, so the exact row number doesn't matter electrically.

Each pot has its wiper on one side of the breadboard centre gap (9t.e / 15t.e). Its two outer legs are on the other side (8b.f/10b.f and 14b.f/16b.f), and short black and red jumpers take those legs to the - and + rails.

graph_initial.title: 8x8 LED Matrix Row-Column Scanning
notes: Parts are the same as step 1. Only the labels of wire3 and wire4 changed. In the circuit image the upper pot (pot1) goes to A1 and the lower pot (pot2) goes to A0. Step 1 had them the other way round.

Matrix pin mapping comes from the manual's table, converted to the catalogue's R/C names: pin1=R5(13), pin2=R7(12), pin3=C2(11), pin4=C3(10), pin5=R8(A2), pin6=C5(A3), pin7=R6(A4), pin8=R3(A5), pin9=R1(2), pin10=C4(3), pin11=C6(4), pin12=R4(5), pin13=C1(6), pin14=R2(7), pin15=C7(8), pin16=C8(9).
The 8 resistors (the yellow leads in the image) are in series on Arduino pins 2-9. Each goes straight to its matrix pin. Pins 10-13 and A2-A5 use the green jumper wires with no resistor, as drawn.

The image shows the breadboard rotated, with rows numbered down the side. I read its right-hand rails as 'tp' (+) and 'tn' (-), at the row numbers where the wires land. Rails are single strips, so the exact row number doesn't matter electrically.

Each pot has its wiper on one side of the breadboard centre gap (9t.e / 15t.e). Its two outer legs are on the other side (8b.f/10b.f and 14b.f/16b.f). Short black and red jumpers take those legs to the - and + rails.
The Uno's GND.1 is used for the ground wire. The image shows it going to a GND pin on the power header.
